description: Track what this add-on bundles: Grafana Alloy, the Home Assistant base image, the GitHub Actions and the Loki used in CI. EVERY bump automerges once CI is green - and CI runs the built image under the AppArmor profile in enforce mode against a real journal and a real Loki, so a release that needs a path the profile does not grant, or that breaks the journal reader, never merges. A merge publishes an image; Home Assistant installs it through the add-on's auto-update.

customManagers.description: ALLOY_VERSION in the Dockerfile follows grafana/alloy releases

The add-on version IS the Alloy version, so config.yaml moves with the same release. No ^ anchor: without a multiline flag it only matched at file start, and the file starts with a comment - Renovate's first PR bumped the Dockerfile alone.

packageRules.description: One PR per Alloy release, touching Dockerfile and config.yaml together
Alloy bumps of every size automerge after the e2e gate; a release must be 3 days old first, so one Grafana pulls or hotfixes in its first days never lands
Base image tags look like trixie-2026.08.0: track the date part within the trixie line; automerges after the e2e gate rebuilds on it
Pin the builder actions to their release tags, not a floating branch
GitHub Actions and the CI Loki image automerge after CI
